To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 70-kDa member of the hsp70 family, the 73-kD peptide recognition protein, promotes lysosomal degradation of intracel- lular proteins during serum withdrawal and binds to a variety proteins and peptides whose degradation is increased under these conditions.

a 73-kDa member of the hsp70 family, isolated by affinity with RNase S- peptide-Sepharose, binds to a variety proteins and peptides whose lysosomal degradation is increased during serum withdrawal and promotes the degradation of these proteins and peptides in lysosomes in vitro.

a member of the hsp70 family of proteins, hsc73, binds to several proteins that are degraded at an increased rate during serum withdrawal, and hsc73 promotes the degradation of these proteins and of RNase S-peptides in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which hsp70s stimulate intracellular proteolysis during serum withdrawal.
the mechanism of protein degradation during starvation.
the identification and characterization of a protein, prp73, that binds to proteins and peptides and that promotes their degradation by lysosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 73-kD peptide binding protein isolated by affinity chromatograpy with RNase S- peptide is the heat shock protein of 73-kDa.
prp73 and the hsc73 protein are the same.
the 73-kD protein that binds to RNase peptide is the hsc73 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prp73 (hsc73) binds to proteins and peptides and promotes their uptake and degradation by lysosomes.

prp73, a member of the hsc73 family, binds to a variety proteins and peptides, including the pentapeptide KFERQ, which are degraded during serum withdrawal, and that prp73 and its homologue, hsc73, promote uptake and degradation by lysosomes.
prp73, the 73-kDA heat shock cognate, is a protein binding protein which binds to a variety proteins, including the 73-kD protein itself, and promotes the lysosomal degradation of these proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hsc73 is a peptide binding protein that stimulates lysosomal proteolyses in vitro and may play a similar role in vivo.
the 70-kDA heat shock cognate (Hsc70) protein binds to a wide variety of proteins and peptides and stimulates the degradation of intracellular protein by lysosomes.
prp73, which we now refer to as hsc73, is a member of the hsc70 family that binds to a variety or proteins and peptides, including those whose degradation rates are increased during starvation.
